setup: Lie on a flat bench, one dumbbell
Feet wide and flat on the floor
Free hand on the bench or held up
execution: Brace so your body doesn't tip
Lower to chest level, elbow about 45°
faults: Don't let your hips or torso roll
Don't flare your elbow out wide
Don't let the weight drift to the floor

notes: Start lighter than your two-dumbbell press: the trunk has to stop you rolling off the bench.
Set the dumbbell down by bringing it to your chest and sitting up, not by dropping it to the side.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Dumbbell bench press
regressions.reason: Two dumbbells balance each other, so there's no rotation to resist.

regressions.name: Dumbbell floor press
regressions.reason: Floor support and a shorter range.

progressions.name: Single-arm press with feet off the floor
progressions.reason: Removes the foot base so the trunk works harder.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell bench press
substitutions.reason: Both arms at once; heavier total load.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Anti-rotation core work without the press.

substitutions.name: Landmine press
substitutions.reason: One-arm press standing; also trains the trunk.

substitutions.name: Chest press machine
substitutions.reason: Supported pressing; can be done one arm at a time.

guideBrief.cameraNote: End-on view from the foot of the bench, camera slightly raised, so the level shoulders and hips (no tipping toward the loaded side) are clear.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Lying on a flat bench, feet wide. One dumbbell held over the shoulder with the arm straight; free hand gripping the bench edge. Shoulders and hips level.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Dumbbell lowered to chest level beside the chest, elbow about 45° from the body and below the bench line. Torso still flat; no roll toward the loaded side.

ikHints: Back and hips stay on the bench
guideBrief.barPath: Dumbbell moves up and down over the shoulder in a slight arc
emphasise: Torso stays level against the one-sided load
